project.title: Virgin Galactic - Dogstudio
project.format: scroll-and-swipe WebGL journey through a 3D spacecraft story

why: A strong motion reference for making a technical product story feel spatial without turning the interface into a passive film: Dogstudio combines linked WebGL subscenes, a 3D spacecraft sequence, and scroll-or-swipe transitions with conventional CMS content surfaces.

compositions.title: Linked WebGL subscenes
compositions.study: Dogstudio describes a multi-scene WebGL system that moves visitors through the flight narrative rather than presenting one isolated hero animation.
compositions.reuse: Split a long 3D story into purposeful scenes with explicit content beats instead of treating the canvas as decoration.

compositions.title: Spaceflight steps paired with CMS content
compositions.study: The case pairs the 3D experience with ordinary editorial and card content, so the story has readable anchors beyond the immersive moments.
compositions.reuse: Keep explanatory copy and conventional navigation available alongside spatial scenes.

assets.notes: The case documents a 3D spacecraft sequence inside multiple WebGL subscenes.
assets.reuse: Reserve real-time 3D for a specific narrative object, then let standard content carry the supporting detail.

assets.notes: The case describes CMS-backed content surfaces around the interactive flight sequence.
assets.reuse: Use managed content to keep an immersive campaign maintainable after its launch sequence is built.

motion.title: Scroll-or-swipe scene transitions
motion.notes: The case documents event-driven scroll and swipe animation, including a two-way pinning and clipping transition between scenes.
motion.fallback: Reduced-motion support was not verified in the source. Reuse only with a readable linear path and direct scene links that do not depend on gesture animation.

motion.title: Performance-bounded environment motion
motion.notes: Dogstudio avoided real-time reflections that would degrade lower-power devices, substituting precomputed 360-degree environment maps at much lower cost.
motion.fallback: Offer a static or low-cost scene treatment for constrained devices; this is performance evidence, not verified reduced-motion support.

interactions.title: Two-way gesture-driven flight progression
interactions.study: Scroll and swipe gestures both advance and reverse the 3D flight sequence, with pinned and clipped transitions connecting subscenes.
interactions.reuse: When gestures drive a narrative, make reverse travel as coherent as forward travel and preserve non-gesture controls.

interactions.title: Event-driven WebGL scene system
interactions.study: Dogstudio credits a complex front-end and WebGL event system rather than one self-running visual sequence.
interactions.reuse: Model interactive scenes as explicit state transitions so content, loading, and escape paths remain controllable.

implementation.format: Dogstudio WebGL case-study experience with multi-scene 3D, scroll/swipe event transitions, and CMS content
implementation.notes: First-party case-study inspection confirmed Dogstudio's Virgin Galactic collaboration, named motion-design credits, multiple WebGL subscenes, a 3D spacecraft sequence, two-way pinning and clipping transitions, and a lower-power reflection strategy. Accessibility and reduced-motion behavior were not verified.
